cast_by: the ruling gate (2026-08-04-the-shim-routes-everything) — no /intent firing behind it, because a ruling that changes the spec is not a newly-born intention; the design was decided at Akien's gate and what is owed is the code catching up
intent: Delete system_rackmount's broker — ADVERTISED, subscribe(), _resolve(), _subs, subscription_probes() — leaving it the owner of the host READING only, and move the predicate home: a device that wants a line on a host resource declares its own Probe and its own shim fires it.
why: Akien, 2026-08-04: 'each device should own it's own everything as much as possible, that's encapsulation. SO RULED.' The broker had one device holding other devices' predicates, which is the opposite; it also ran a SECOND firing path parallel to the one every BaseShim already has, so the deletion is a simplification and not a trade. The Law 6 claim that justified it ('the raw reading never leaves the device') was never Law 6 — Law 6 gates writes.
red_it_answers: cairn/system_rackmount is RED under Law 9 as of 2026-08-04: its charter describes the ruled design and its code ships the broker. Named in the charter's `red` field.
falsifier: DONE when a real consumer device declares a host-resource probe in its OWN shim, that probe fires on the beat, and system_rackmount holds no table keyed by another device's address — measured by the consumer's proof, not by system_rackmount's. WRONG if the deletion just relocates the broker (e.g. a shared helper that registers predicates for callers is the same shape wearing a module name), or if removing the subscription table leaves no way for a device to read the host at all — the READING must survive; only the protocol around it dies.

BUILDME.need: the capstone proof (proofs/test_system_rackmount.py) is rewritten, not patched — it currently seals advertise/subscribe/poke end to end, including the Law-6 leak-check whose premise the ruling retires. A proof that keeps passing after the design it proves is deleted is the hollow kind (Law 8).

a real consumer names itself. Today NOTHING subscribes — the broker was built for a hypothetical caller, which is part of why the wrong shape survived. The rework should land with the first device that actually wants a host line, so the new shape is measured rather than asserted (Law 3).

PROVEME.need: cairn/system_rackmount/history.json records the identity correction — this is the SECOND one for this device (scheduler -> owner-of-predicates 2026-07-18, owner-of-predicates -> owner-of-the-reading 2026-08-04) and the pair is the evidence, not the individual entries.

watchme: A probe created at the crossing, aimed at the falsifier's second clause: report back whether the broker reappeared anywhere in the corpus under a different name (a registration helper, a predicate registry, a shared subscribe module). The shape is what recurs, not the identifier — this is the fourth reify-vs-flow catch recorded in I-heartbeat-probes-and-bus.md, and the first three all came back at least once under new spelling.
